description: The endpoint checks authentication and a broad role, but not that the caller owns the key id.
The new plaintext key is returned in a URL/query parameter, exposing it to logs, caches, and referrers.

match: ((immediate|no grace|without grace|grace period).{0,80}(revoke|old key)|(revoke|old key).{0,80}(immediate|no grace|grace|rollback|breaking)|no.*transition|rollback plan)
description: The old key is revoked immediately with no grace period or rollback, so integrations break during rollout.
A state-changing rotation uses GET, so prefetch, retries, and caches can trigger it.

match: ((no|missing|without|lacks|lack of).{0,60}(idempoten|idempotency key|lock)|(idempoten|idempotency).{0,60}(missing|not implemented|no key|lacks|without)|\b(double|retry|concurrent|race)\b.{0,80}(rotation|key|request)|two rotations|first new key|lost response)
description: There is no idempotency key or per-key lock; a retry or double submit can create two valid keys or race the revoke.
